evidence: src/application/errors/ApplicationError.ts: abstract class ApplicationError with subclasses ValidationError, NotFoundError(resource, id) and ConflictError. This is the module's error type set.

src/application/errors/errorClassification.ts: classifyError(error: unknown): ClassifiedError is the only place that maps errors to ErrorKind and code (INVALID_INPUT, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, INSUFFICIENT_STOCK, INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION, INTERNAL_ERROR).
errorClassification.ts imports ConflictError, NotFoundError and ValidationError from './ApplicationError' and checks them with instanceof, so it uses the module's own types directly.
The NotFoundError message template `${resource} ${id} not found` is defined only in its constructor and is not rebuilt in classifyError.

Incoming: use cases (AddProductUseCase, lookups, orderCommandParsers, inputGuards, ListOrdersUseCase) import ApplicationError.ts, and infrastructure/http/middleware/errorHandler.ts imports errorClassification.ts. Each file has a separate, consistent role.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module passes. Both files deal with one concern: application-level failures. ApplicationError.ts defines the error types (an abstract ApplicationError base plus ValidationError, NotFoundError and ConflictError). errorClassification.ts converts those errors, and the relevant domain errors, into a ClassifiedError that does not depend on any transport.

No rule is duplicated:
- The NotFoundError message format is built only in its own constructor.
- The mapping from an error to its kind and code exists only in classifyError.

classifyError checks the module's own error classes with instanceof rather than matching names or strings, so it doesn't work around the module's own types. Incoming edges back this split: use cases import the error types, and the HTTP error handler imports only classifyError. That shows each file has a clear role within the module's boundary. The import of domain errors is an import-direction question, which is out of scope here.
